name: Field Finder for ACF
author: Jaydip Makwana

sections.description:
Field Finder for ACF is a developer tool. It scans your code and shows exactly where an Advanced Custom Field is read or written.

Find a field

  • Search by field name, field key (field_…) or pattern such as hero_*
  • Field name suggestions with label, type and field group
  • File, line number and code snippet for every match
  • Detects get_field, the_field, get_sub_field, the_sub_field, have_rows, get_field_object, update_field, delete_field, add_row and more
  • Detects [acf field="…"] shortcodes in code and, optionally, in post content
  • Ignores commented-out code
  • Lists dynamic calls such as get_field( $name ) separately, because they cannot be checked

Unused fields report

Lists every ACF field with how often it appears in your code. Fields with no matches are shown first.

Scan scope

Active theme, parent theme, plugins, must-use plugins or a custom folder. Optionally scan Twig templates and ACF block.json example data.

Built for large sites

  • Scans in batches with a progress bar, so it does not time out
  • Caches results per file (by modified time), so repeat searches are fast
  • Skips node_modules, vendor, .git and very large files

Export and CLI

  • Download results as CSV or JSON
  • WP-CLI: wp field-finder search <field>, wp field-finder unused, wp field-finder clear-cache

Developer hooks

  • fielffoa_functions – ACF function names to look for
  • fielffoa_excluded_dirs – folder names to skip
  • fielffoa_max_file_size – largest file (bytes) to parse
  • fielffoa_scan_roots – folders to scan
  • fielffoa_batch_seconds – seconds spent per AJAX batch
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu
  3. Go to Tools > Field Finder for ACF
sections.faq:
Does it need ACF?

Searching code works without ACF. Field name suggestions and the unused fields report need ACF (free or Pro) to be active.

Why is a field marked “Possibly used”?

It is a sub field of a Group or Clone field, and the parent field is used in code. Those values are normally read through the parent.

Why might an unused field actually be used?

Fields read through dynamic names (for example get_field( $prefix . '_title' )), by other plugins outside the scanned folders, or by page builders. The report shows how many dynamic calls it could not check.

Is anything sent to an external service?

No. Everything runs on your server.

Multisite?

Each site scans its own active theme. Only super admins can scan plugins, must-use plugins or custom folders.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • New: unused fields report
  • New: field name suggestions
  • New: file, line number and code snippet for every match
  • New: scan the parent theme, plugins, must-use plugins or a custom folder
  • New: Twig templates, ACF block.json and [acf] shortcodes (code and post content)
  • New: batched AJAX scanning with progress bar and per-file cache
  • New: CSV and JSON export
  • New: WP-CLI commands
  • New: token based PHP parsing, so commented-out code is ignored
  • New: dynamic calls are listed separately
  • Fix: field names containing regex characters no longer break the search
  • Fix: Windows paths
  • Fix: stylesheet version now follows the plugin version
  • Security: nonce and capability checks on every request; custom folders must be inside the WordPress install
  • New: redesigned interface with a search bar, scope chips, editor-style code panels and a status filter for the unused fields report
  • Improved: translatable strings, follows the admin colour scheme, linkable search URLs
  • Uninstall now removes cached data

1.0.1

  • Improved UI with modern design elements and smoother interactions

1.0

  • Initial release
